title: PMS discovery questions
objectives: Ask the five PMS discovery questions.
Test drawdown tolerance with the 30% question.
body_md:
- "What share of your total investments would this ₹50 lakh be?"
- "What did you do with your equity investments in March 2020?"
- "If this portfolio fell 30% in a year while the Nifty fell 15%, how would you react?"
- "Do you need any of this money in the next three years?"
- "Do you have stocks or sectors you want excluded, for example your employer's shares?"

> **Investor takeaway:** PMS is not a better mutual fund. It suits investors who already have a core portfolio and can handle bigger swings.
example: You ask, 'What did you do with your equity in March 2020?' The client says he sold half. You note a lower drawdown tolerance and set expectations before PMS.
say: If this portfolio fell 30% in a year while the Nifty fell 15%, how would you react?
Do you have any stocks you would want excluded?

check.q: Which discovery question best tests drawdown tolerance?
o: "Which PMS did your friend invest in?"
"What did you do with your equity investments in March 2020?"
check.why: Past behaviour in a real fall reveals tolerance. Also ask how they'd react to a 30% fall while the Nifty fell 15%.

check.q: A client expects PMS to defer tax like a mutual fund. What should you explain?
o: PMS is tax-free for ₹50 lakh+ investors
Every trade by the manager is a tax event in the client's hands
Tax is paid only on final exit
The PMS provider pays the tax
check.why: Expecting MF-like deferral is a suitability red flag. High turnover can mean a bigger tax bill.

check.q: Why ask whether the client holds employer shares?
o: To plan a stock exclusion and avoid concentration
check.why: PMS can allow stock exclusions, and a client may want to avoid more of their employer's shares.
